1. This  is  a  petition  for  quashing  of  the  proceedings 
pending vide S.C.C.No.28897 of 2024 before the J.M.F .C., Thane, 
arising out of the C.R.No.1223 of 2024, registered at Kasarvadavli 
police  station,  on  28.07.2024,  under  sections  329(3),  115(2), 
324(4),  352,  351(1)  and  3(5)  of  the  Bhartiya  Nyaya  Sanhita, 
2023.
2. Heard Mr. Ashok Kumar Shukla, learned counsel for the 
Petitioners,  Mr.  Yagnik,  learned  APP  for  the  State  and  Mr .

Siddharth Singh, learned counsel for the Respondent No.2.
3. The F .I.R. is lodged by the Respondent No.2. His sister 
Priyanka had got married with the Petitioner No.3. The Petiti oner 
No.1  is  the  sister  and  the  Petitioner  Nos.2  is  cousin  of  the  
Petitioner  No.3.  The  matter  is  settled  between  the  parties, 
therefore, it is not necessary to refer to the allegations in the F .I.R. 
in detail. However, the gist of the F .I.R. is that the informant’s sister 
had lodged some cases against the Petitioner No.3 and his family. 
The  incident  in  question  had  occurred  at  09.05p.m.  on 
27.07.2024. At that time, the petitioners entered the informant’s 
house. His sister Priyanka was present in that house as it was her  
parent’s house. All the three petitioners and the 4 th lady who is not 
the party to this petition entered the house and started q uarreling 
with  the  informant  and  his  sister.  They  started  abusing  the 
informant and his family. They also caused some damage to the 
articles in the house. On these allegations, the F .I.R. was lodg ed. 
The charge-sheet contains the statements of the informant’s siste r 
and cousin who have supported the informant’s case.

3 of  4 5-wp-2466-25
4. The Respondent No.2 has filed his Affidavit in reply. He 
has stated in his affidavit that the F .I.R. is lodged because of some 
confusion,  but  the  matter  is  amicably  settled  and  he  has  no 
objection for quashing of the proceedings. 
5. The Respondent No.2 is present before the Court. He is 
identified by his learned counsel. He reiterated the con tents of the 
affidavit and stated before the Court that he has no objection fo r 
quashing of the proceedings. 
6. The incident appears to be a petty incident. No serious  
damage  was  done.  The  parties  have  settled  their  differences. 
Therefore, we are inclined to allow this petition. It is made clear 
that the 4 th accused is not before the Court, but considering the 
over all settlement, the proceedings are quashed in totality. 
7. Hence, the following order:
O R D E R
i) The proceedings pending vide S.C.C.No.28897 of 
2024 before the J.M.F .C., Thane, arising out of 
the  C.R.No.1223  of  2024,  registered  at

4 of  4 5-wp-2466-25
Kasarvadavli police station, on 28.07.2024, under 
sections 329(3), 115(2), 324(4), 352, 351(1) and 
3(5) of the Bhartiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, are 
quashed and set aside. 
ii) The writ petition is disposed of. 
(S. M. MODAK, J.)  (SARANG V. KOTWAL, J.)
